title: Minimum Meeting Rooms
statement: You are given a list of meeting time intervals where each interval is [start, end] (a meeting occupies the half-open range [start, end)). Return the minimum number of conference rooms required to hold all the meetings without any overlap.
reference_solution:
def min_meeting_rooms(intervals):
    if not intervals:
        return 0
    starts = sorted(i[0] for i in intervals)
    ends = sorted(i[1] for i in intervals)
    rooms = 0
    max_rooms = 0
    s = e = 0
    n = len(intervals)
    while s < n:
        if starts[s] < ends[e]:
            rooms += 1
            s += 1
            max_rooms = max(max_rooms, rooms)
        else:
            rooms -= 1
            e += 1
    return max_rooms
hints: Think about tracking, at every moment in time, how many meetings are currently in progress simultaneously.
Sorting starts and ends separately lets you sweep through time events in order without building a full timeline.

Sort start times and end times independently. Walk through starts with a pointer; whenever the next start is before the earliest unfreed end, you need a new room (increment and track the max); otherwise a room frees up (advance the end pointer) before adding the new meeting.
